subject: Motive Labs expansion — usage reconciliation and burst coverage proposal
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex@motivelabs.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
Cc: procurement@motive.com
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Request: short-term GPU expansion and usage reconciliation

Neha,

Thanks for the partnership — we've been ramping up a new multimodal retrieval workload and consumption blew past our forecast for Q3. We're seeing sustained 2.2x higher token throughput on the H100 pool for the last six weeks and it's impacting our SLAs (95th p95 latency spikes). Can Redwood help with a short-term expansion while we renegotiate commits?

What we need:
- ~10–14 additional H100-equivalent slots for 6–8 weeks (burst pool or dedicated tranche)
- A simple usage reconciliation doc so our finance team can map overage to the upcoming renewal

Open to pricing options: surge credits, short-term flat fee, or a one-off top-up applied against a renewed commit. Can you advise ASAP — our CTO asked for options by EOD tomorrow.

Attached: brief usage snapshot (CSV) from our side.

Appreciate it,
Alex Moreno
Head of ML Infrastructure
Motive Labs

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
To: Alex Moreno <alex@motivelabs.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, ben_carter@redwood.example.com, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: short-term GPU expansion and usage reconciliation

Thanks Alex — and thanks for the CSV. I pulled together a quick intake and opened this thread to loop in karthik (capacity) and Ben (commercial).

Short answers up front: yes, we can support a time-bound tranche and provide a reconciliation that feeds into your renewal. Below is the approach we recommend for a fast, low-friction outcome:

1) Immediate temporary burst: provision a 12-slot H100 burst tranche scoped for 8 weeks. This runs in a dedicated pool with thermal headroom and pre-warmed KV caches to avoid cold start latency.
2) Usage reconciliation: we'll generate a reconciliation report that maps actual consumed GPU-hours and token throughput to unit economics, and credit any agreed overage toward the renewal commit.
3) Operational guardrails: set a per-minute throttle and auto-fallback to a lower-cost L4 variant for non-critical traffic to protect latency SLOs.

I've attached the CSV you sent and a blank reconciliation template (motive_capacity_snapshot_q3.csv). Karthik — can you confirm thermal/slot availability next week and an ETA for provisioning? Ben — will need guidance on pricing tiers (surge-credit vs flat top-up) and DocuSign SOW options.

Next steps: karthik to respond with provisioning ETA + any ops caveats; Ben to propose commercial options by EOD. I'll coordinate the reconciliation template and schedule a 30-min call if needed.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com, Alex Moreno <alex@motivelabs.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example.com, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 13:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: short-term GPU expansion and usage reconciliation

Hi all — quick capacity note from the infra side.

Summary recommendation (ops):
- Provision: 12 H100-equivalent slots in a dedicated short-lived tranche (8 weeks). This aligns with the 2.2x uplift reported and gives ~30% buffer for variability.
- Hot-standby: allocate a 2-slot hot-standby pool for failover to maintain p95 during rolling maintenance or preemption events.
- Thermal headroom: confirm we can place tranche in DC West-2 with a 20% thermal reserve; if Motive requires a specific region we'll need 36–48 hrs more for placement.
- Config: pre-seed KV caches and set batch window to 40ms for generation workloads; enable prefix caching for the top 10 request patterns you shared.

Operational caveats:
- Billing granularity: we bill by GPU-hour with minute-level granularity; we'll produce an hourly dump for reconciliation.
- Model variant fallback: recommend fallback to a cheaper L4 variant for non-SLA traffic during peak minutes — reduces cost by ~45% for those requests.

If this works, ops can provision within 6 business hours for West-2, or next-day for constrained placements. I attached a one-page capacity snapshot and the proposed SOW draft (proposed_sow_draft.pdf) for Ben to review commercial terms.

-Karthik
Head, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: short-term GPU expansion and usage reconciliation

Thanks team — Ben here. Commercial option summary for Motive Labs (DEAL-4821):

Option A — Surge credits (recommended for speed):
- One-off purchase of 8,000 surge credits (covers ~12 H100 slots for 8 weeks at your avg usage profile).
- Credits applied immediately; any unused credits roll into renewal as a 75% credit toward committed term.
- Advantages: fastest to provision, minimal paperwork.

Option B — Flat top-up with reconciliation:
- Fixed fee for 8-week tranche invoiced up-front; we produce a reconciliation report at period end and apply agreed overage credits to the renewal.
- Advantages: simpler accounting for Motive Finance.

Option C — Temp commit amendment:
- Short-term amendment to commit (month-to-month) with stepped pricing and guaranteed slot reservation.
- Advantages: predictability; requires signature on SOW (DocuSign link below).

Recommendation: go with Option A to get capacity up within hours. If Motive prefers straight invoicing, Option B is acceptable. I'll prepare a 1-page SOW and DocuSign envelope after you confirm.

DocuSign (proposed SOW): https://www.docusign.com/en/link/ENVELOPE-9f3b2e
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-4821

Alex — can you confirm preferred option and whether Motive wants the tranche in US-West region? If yes, ops will kick off provisioning today.
